leads.title: Tailored skin clothing of the North American Arctic
leads.where: Bering Strait, Arctic Canada and Greenland
leads.why: Double-layer caribou parkas, waterproof gut coats and sealed boots made permanent life possible on the Arctic coast and sea ice.
leads.verify: The oldest preserved skin clothing and sewing gear in the American Arctic (for example the Saqqaq finds from Qeqertasussuk, Greenland); what was carried from Siberia and what was developed in place; the Thule-period garments.
search: Inuit skin clothing history waterproof stitch gut parka
Paleo-Inuit needles sewing Arctic Small Tool tradition

leads.title: Fat-burning stone lamps in Ice Age Europe
leads.why: A hollowed stone with animal fat and a plant wick gave steady light away from the hearth, used for work at night and deep inside painted caves.
leads.verify: The earliest securely dated stone lamps and how many are known; residue evidence for fuels and wicks; whether lamps elsewhere (the Arctic, the Near East) are separate origins.
search: de Beaune Paleolithic lamps and their specialization Current Anthropology 1987
earliest Aurignacian lamp fat burning evidence

leads.title: Ondol underfloor heating in Korea
leads.where: Northern Korean peninsula and the neighbouring coast
leads.why: Flues from the kitchen fire running under a stone floor heated Korean houses through the winter, and the heated floor is still the standard there.
leads.verify: The earliest excavated flue-heated floors in Korea and the Russian Far East and their dates; the relation to the Chinese kang; the Greek and Roman hypocaust (from about the third century BCE), which is a separate origin and may be the earlier one.
search: earliest ondol gudeul archaeological evidence Okjeo Krounovka
history of ondol Korean underfloor heating origins
hypocaust origin Greek baths third century BCE

leads.title: The hammock in tropical America
leads.where: Northern South America and the Caribbean
leads.why: A woven hanging bed kept sleepers clear of damp and vermin across the American tropics, and Europe's navies used it to berth their crews for three centuries.
leads.verify: The first European descriptions (Columbus 1492, Oviedo) and what they establish; any archaeological or linguistic evidence for its age and place of origin, since the year given here is only a placeholder; its adoption at sea.
search: pre-Columbian hammock archaeological evidence South America

leads.title: The electric washing machine
leads.where: Chicago and the United States Midwest
leads.why: Powered washing removed the heaviest weekly task of housework and freed, in time, billions of hours of mostly women's labour.
leads.verify: The first electric machines sold and their makers (the Thor of the Hurley company and rivals), since priority is disputed; the hand-cranked drum machines before them; rates of household adoption through the century.
search: first electric washing machine Thor Hurley 1907 Alva Fisher patent
history of washing machine invention priority
Cowan More Work for Mother household technology

leads.title: The sweat bath in Mesoamerica
leads.why: Masonry steam rooms served washing, childbirth and healing in Mesoamerican towns for three thousand years and are still in use.
leads.verify: The earliest excavated sweat bath (reported at Cuello, Belize, about 900 BCE) and later examples; its uses as recorded in the sixteenth century; the unrelated bathhouses of the Old World (Greek and Roman baths, the sauna) and the sweat lodges of North America as separate origins.
